page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression, falls into the bottom 25 percent tier. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads demonstrate average tier performance, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core CPU and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations, consistently place in the middle 50 percent tier. Geekbench scores for software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing also align with this average performance profile.

From a resource allocation perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power without resource contention. Given the average multi-core processing, database operations, and static web serving throughput benchmarks, this instance is suitable for multi-threaded applications, web serving, software compilation, and database operations that fit within the 64.0 GB memory limit.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Utilizing the KVM hypervisor, this instance allocates 2.0 GB of memory per core and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps, with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark data reveals a contrast between weak single-core performance and average multi-core execution, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests consistently placing in the middle 50 percent tier. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform at average levels. This resource profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy, multi-threaded workloads that do not demand high memory-to-CPU ratios. It is suitable for web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale database operations.
